findings.description: Changing `if fg is not None` to `if fg:` makes falsy colors be skipped. Color 0 (black in the 256-color palette) is silently ignored, and the same holds for `bg` at line 684.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg=0)` or `bg=0`. `0` is falsy, so no escape code is emitted and the text is rendered in the default color instead of the requested one. The user gets silently wrong output.

findings.description: The validation in `_interpret_color` was removed. Out-of-range ints, malformed tuples, and bools are no longer rejected.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `fg=300`, `fg=(1,2)`, or `fg=(300,0,0)`. Ints and tuples are formatted directly into the escape sequence, so invalid ANSI codes are emitted with no error. A 2-element tuple raises an unpacking ValueError. An unhashable value reaching the dict lookup raises TypeError.
